title: PAY-142 payment retry
mode_reason: payments and persistence are critical areas and money is irreversible

references.title: PAY-142 Retry charges on provider timeout
references.relevance: retry limit and the never-charge-twice rule

intent.stated: Retry a timed-out charge up to three times; never charge a buyer twice; keep local status converging with the provider ledger.
intent.reconstructed: Bounded retry loop with a fresh idempotency key per attempt, an attempt row per try, and no applied-once guard in the events consumer.
divergences: REF-1 forbids a second charge, but src/payments/retry.py:11 generates a new idempotency key per attempt so the provider cannot deduplicate (REF-3).
The PR calls the consumer change a simplification; REF-2 invariant I-3 requires idempotent consumers under at-least-once delivery (REF-4).
Neither source describes reconciliation for attempts that time out after the provider already charged.

changed_surface.summary: retry loop, per-attempt idempotency key, attempt rows
one row per attempt, no uniqueness on order_id

affected_surface.why: retry reaches the provider with a different key
status is written only on the success path

risks.title: Double charge after a retried timeout
risks.mechanism: Provider charges successfully, the response times out, the loop generates a fresh idempotency key at retry.py:11 and charges again; the provider sees two distinct keys and cannot deduplicate.
risks.invariant: I-1 one order produces at most one provider charge
risks.detectability: invisible locally; only the provider ledger shows both charges
risks.blast_radius: every timed-out charge, about 0.4% of all charges per REF-1
risks.existing_protection: none; the stable per-order key was removed by this diff

risks.title: Local status stuck in PENDING after an ambiguous timeout
risks.mechanism: All three attempts time out while one actually charged; the success branch never runs so the UPDATE at retry.py:18 never executes and the row stays PENDING.
risks.invariant: I-2 local status converges with the provider ledger
risks.blast_radius: orders whose final attempt is ambiguous
risks.existing_protection: hourly reconciliation job, but see RISK-004

risks.title: Duplicate ledger rows on event redelivery
risks.mechanism: handle_payment_event applies the update and the ledger insert unconditionally; at-least-once delivery replays the event and inserts a second ledger row.
risks.invariant: I-3 consumers are idempotent under at-least-once delivery
risks.detectability: ledger totals drift from provider totals
risks.existing_protection: none after this diff removed the applied-once guard

risks.title: Reconciliation cannot see ambiguous attempts
risks.mechanism: The reconciliation job reads the payments table only; an attempt that charged but never updated payments leaves no signal it can act on, so RISK-002 is not repaired.
risks.invariant: I-2 local status converges within one reconciliation cycle
risks.detectability: only by comparing provider ledger totals with payments
risks.existing_protection: none; payment_requests is written but never read

risks.title: Three immediate attempts amplify a provider incident
risks.mechanism: The loop retries with no backoff, so a provider slowdown triples request volume.
risks.existing_protection: provider-side rate limiting returns 429, which is not retried

cases.title: Lost response after a successful charge must not produce a second charge
cases.objective: After the provider charges and the response is lost, does the retry create a second charge?
cases.why_it_catches_the_risk: It forces the exact ambiguous-timeout path where retry.py:11 mints a new idempotency key, which is the mechanism of RISK-001.
preconditions: Sandbox merchant account with an empty ledger
Order ORD-1 exists in status CREATED with amount 1000

environment.services: payments-api and provider sandbox via docker compose up -d

fixtures: Order ORD-1, amount 1000, card 4111111111111111, merchant_ref ORD-1
fault_injection: toxiproxy rule pay-timeout: allow the request, drop the response after 100 ms, applied to attempt 1 only

steps.action: Enable the toxiproxy rule pay-timeout limited to the first provider call, then POST /payments with order_id=ORD-1 amount=1000
steps.expected: The provider records exactly one charge for ORD-1 and the client observes a timeout
steps.how_to_observe: GET http://provider-sandbox/ledger?merchant_ref=ORD-1 returns 1 entry; client response is HTTP 504

steps.action: Observe the attempt rows before the retry fires
steps.expected: payment_requests has exactly one row for ORD-1 with attempt=0 and a non-null idempotency_key
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT attempt, idempotency_key FROM payment_requests WHERE order_id='ORD-1' ORDER BY attempt

steps.action: Disable the toxiproxy rule and let the retry loop run to completion
steps.expected: The retry reaches the provider with a different idempotency key and the provider creates a second charge
steps.how_to_observe: GET http://provider-sandbox/ledger?merchant_ref=ORD-1 and compare entry count and keys with step 1

steps.expected: payments.status for ORD-1 is SUCCEEDED and payment_requests holds two rows with different keys
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT status FROM payments WHERE order_id='ORD-1'; SELECT count(*), count(distinct idempotency_key) FROM payment_requests WHERE order_id='ORD-1'

intermediate_checks: After step 2 the payments row is still PENDING, proving the retry has not yet run
The two attempt rows must be compared by idempotency_key, not by count alone
expected_final_state: The provider ledger holds exactly one entry of 1000 for merchant_ref ORD-1
Every payment_requests row for ORD-1 carries the same idempotency_key
forbidden_outcomes: Two or more provider ledger entries for ORD-1
Two payment_requests rows with different idempotency_key values
payments.status SUCCEEDED while the ledger holds zero entries

oracle.expected: exactly one entry, amount 1000, status captured

cleanup: Refund or void every sandbox charge for ORD-1
cases.flake_policy: An inconsistent result across repetitions is a defect, not a flake: capture the ledger and all attempt rows and stop the run.

cases.title: All attempts time out after a real charge leaves a converging status
cases.objective: When every attempt times out but the provider charged once, does the local status converge?
cases.why_it_catches_the_risk: It drives the branch where the success path at retry.py:18 never executes, which is the mechanism of RISK-002.
preconditions: Order ORD-2 in CREATED with amount 500

environment.services: payments-api, provider sandbox, reconciliation worker stopped

fault_injection: toxiproxy drops every provider response for ORD-2 while allowing the requests through

steps.action: POST /payments for ORD-2 with the drop rule active
steps.expected: The provider records at least one charge and every attempt times out

steps.action: Wait for the loop to exhaust MAX_ATTEMPTS and observe the local row
steps.expected: payments.status for ORD-2 is PENDING and the API returned an error
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT status FROM payments WHERE order_id='ORD-2'

steps.action: Start the reconciliation job and let one full cycle finish
steps.expected: The job resolves ORD-2 against the provider ledger and the status stops being PENDING
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT status FROM payments WHERE order_id='ORD-2' after the cycle; reconciliation log line reconcile.resolved order=ORD-2

intermediate_checks: payment_requests holds three rows for ORD-2 before reconciliation runs
expected_final_state: payments.status for ORD-2 is SUCCEEDED or FAILED, matching the provider ledger
The provider ledger and the local status agree
forbidden_outcomes: payments.status remains PENDING after a completed reconciliation cycle

oracle.source: payments table compared with the provider ledger
oracle.query: SELECT status FROM payments WHERE order_id='ORD-2'
oracle.expected: SUCCEEDED when the ledger holds a charge, FAILED when it holds none

cases.side_effect_count: at most 1 provider charge and 0 additional charges during recovery
cleanup: Refund the sandbox charge for ORD-2
Restart the reconciliation worker in its normal configuration
cases.flake_policy: Retry once if the reconciliation cycle did not complete; a second non-converging result is a defect.

cases.title: Redelivered payment event must not duplicate the ledger row
cases.objective: Does replaying one payment event a second time create a second ledger row?
cases.why_it_catches_the_risk: It replays the exact delivery the consumer at events.py:3 now applies without a guard.
preconditions: ledger holds exactly one row for ORD-3
fault_injection: Replay delivery D-1 through the event replay hook after the first delivery is committed

steps.action: Deliver the payment event for ORD-3 once and wait for the consumer to commit
steps.expected: ledger holds exactly one row for ORD-3 with amount 750
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT count(*), sum(amount) FROM ledger WHERE order_id='ORD-3'

steps.expected: The consumer recognizes the event as already applied and writes nothing
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT count(*), sum(amount) FROM ledger WHERE order_id='ORD-3' after the replay

steps.expected: orders.paid stays true and was not written a second time
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT paid FROM orders WHERE id='ORD-3'; consumer log line event.skipped delivery=D-1

intermediate_checks: Consumer offset advances after both deliveries so the replay really reached the handler
expected_final_state: ledger holds exactly one row of 750 for ORD-3
forbidden_outcomes: A ledger sum of 1500 for ORD-3

oracle.query: SELECT count(*), sum(amount) FROM ledger WHERE order_id='ORD-3'

cases.side_effect_count: exactly 1 ledger row per payment event
cleanup: Reset the consumer offset to its pre-test value
cases.flake_policy: A duplicated row on any repetition is a defect; do not average across runs.

cases.title: Reconciliation must act on attempts recorded only in payment_requests
cases.objective: Can reconciliation repair an order whose only trace of a charge is an attempt row?
cases.why_it_catches_the_risk: It creates the exact state RISK-004 predicts: a charged attempt invisible to a payments-only reconciliation query.
preconditions: One payment_requests row for ORD-4 whose key was charged at the provider
No payments row update for ORD-4
fixtures: ORD-4 attempt row with idempotency_key K-4 charged for 300 at the provider
fault_injection: None; the state is seeded directly to isolate the reconciliation query

steps.expected: The job inspects the provider ledger for every order with an unresolved attempt, including ORD-4
steps.how_to_observe: reconciliation log lines listing the orders inspected in this cycle

steps.expected: payments.status for ORD-4 matches the provider ledger
steps.how_to_observe: SELECT status FROM payments WHERE order_id='ORD-4'

intermediate_checks: The cycle log must name ORD-4; absence of the order in the log is the failure signal
expected_final_state: No additional provider charge was issued
forbidden_outcomes: ORD-4 absent from the reconciliation cycle
A second charge created during recovery

oracle.source: payments table compared with the provider ledger for K-4
oracle.query: SELECT status FROM payments WHERE order_id='ORD-4'

cleanup: Refund the sandbox charge for K-4
cases.flake_policy: A single failure is conclusive because the state is seeded deterministically.

required: toxiproxy rule that drops a response after the request is delivered
provider sandbox ledger read access by merchant_ref
event replay hook for a single delivery id
ability to stop and start the reconciliation worker
artifacts/ paths for logs, database snapshots, and reports

missing.request: Add a replay endpoint or test hook that redelivers one payment_event by delivery_id without resetting the whole consumer offset.

execution_plan.rationale: independent of the charge path, runs while the ledger is clean
needs a full reconciliation cycle, so it runs after the fast cases
depends on the seeded state left by CASE-002

open_questions.question: Is a stable per-order idempotency key the intended fix, or does the provider deduplicate by merchant_ref?
open_questions.why: It decides whether RISK-001 is a code defect or a provider-contract assumption, and therefore whether CASE-001 is expected to pass or fail.

waivers.reason: Provider rate limiting returns 429, which this loop does not retry, so amplification is bounded at three attempts per order.
waivers.revisit: if MAX_ATTEMPTS rises above 3 or a backoff-free retry is added elsewhere
